headline: Medium pairwise risk: Prefect can egress workflow metadata while spring-integration-samples has no isolation or verification surfaces, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Prefect has broad network egress, but spring-integration-samples shows no io_surfaces or runnable bridge, so a prompt-injection pathway between them is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a direct ingestion path.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not add shared clipboard or shared workspace mounts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on any future inter-agent channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples has no declared data classes or egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage blast radius appears small, but Prefect could still transmit metadata if connected to external services.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted to the same workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF workflow metadata includes secrets or identifiers, Prefect may exfiltrate them via egress.
mitigations: Store only non-sensitive metadata in shared locations.
Disable external network access for Prefect when processing sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before any outbound call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect exposes broad network egress, but spring-integration-samples declares no write, network, or OAuth scopes and no concurrency model. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface, a capability conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is given write access to the same mutable resource as Prefect, conflict risk becomes possible.
mitigations: requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can emit workflow metadata, and spring-integration-samples is a sample integration repo with no documented verification or action-taking authority. That makes a direct authoritative handoff unlikely, but if B consumes A's outputs as trusted inputs, errors could cascade into downstream automation.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is wired to treat Prefect output as authoritative input, cascading errors become plausible.
IF downstream actions are attached to B, bad metadata can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on Prefect outputs.
Log and review transformed fields before use.
requires-engineering: add human approval for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented. Prefect only lists workflow metadata, and spring-integration-samples lists no data classes or compliance surfaces, so a compliance violation pathway is not evidenced from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent, reassess residency and retention controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
requires-engineering: add compliance classification tags to future workflows.
